definitions.dead(q): 5 - reg(q) - live(q); visited but unregistered, hence unregistrable forever
definitions.live(q): ports of q UNVISITED -- a single-permutation test against hex_masks, never a hexagon popcount
definitions.need(q): ports of q a completion must still register; need(q) <= live(q) always, and the total abandonment slack is 4 - D_dead
definitions.seg_max(q): UPPER bound on ports ONE segment can register in q: a forward +1/+2 walk on the 5-cycle landing only on currently-unvisited ports, displacement <= 4, with every skip given away FREE (the enlarging, sound direction)

vacuity_proof.consequence: ceil(need(q)/seg_max(q)) <= ceil(live(q)/live(q)) = 1 for every orbit, always
vacuity_proof.degeneration: the left side collapses to the number of orbits still needing a segment, so the inequality becomes |Q| + [q0] <= 1 + (R_cap + Phi) -- the Round-71 ORBIT-REENTRY bound with 1 added to BOTH sides
vacuity_proof.method: exhaustive over all 32 live-port masks of a 5-port orbit
vacuity_proof.result: seg_max(q) == |live(q)| for all 32 masks, zero exceptions
vacuity_proof.structural_reason: a forward +1/+2 walk with displacement <= 4 sweeps the entire 5-cycle from a suitably chosen entry: a single dead port is stepped over by +2, and any run of dead ports can be placed behind the entry. With five ports per orbit there is never a live port one segment cannot reach.
vacuity_proof.theorem: no orbit ever needs two segments on within-orbit port-supply grounds

where_a_real_bound_would_live: inter-orbit SEQUENCING, not per-orbit capacity: consecutive segments must be linked by a legal orbit-changing joint, so the orbit sequence is a walk in a fixed digraph on the 144 orbits rather than an unordered selection. All current bounds treat the orbit set as an unordered supply and ignore adjacency entirely. This is a new investigation; nothing here establishes it.
why_not_revivable: the only way to force seg_max(q) < live(q) is to charge the E^2 skips, making seg_max budget-dependent; but R_cap + Phi is a single global budget, so attributing it per orbit is exactly the shared-budget supply-side reasoning retracted in Round 73
